sections.passage:
Isaac Newton (1643-1727) and Albert Einstein (1897-1955) are regarded as two of the most important scientists of all time. They also share some similarities.

Both Einstein and Newton were described as lonely children (22) ________ lacked social skills, but had a passion for complex topics. Einstein dropped out of school at the age of 15 because he felt bored and didn't like the teaching style. (23) ________, Newton didn't excel in school, although he completed his secondary education and managed to enter Cambridge University.

Both worked in the field of physics and maths, but in different time periods and contributed to our (24) ________ of gravity. Newton was the first person to describe gravity and discover the basic laws of mechanics and motion. While Einstein agreed with some aspects of his theory, he showed that Newton was wrong about time and space, and (25) ________ a new theory of gravity. Einstein also established the foundations of modern physics.

The scientific achievements of both Newton and Einstein are impressive, and there is still a debate about who made the bigger (26) ________ to humankind.

[Adapted from Global Success]

Alexander Graham Bell was a Scottish-born scientist and inventor (27) _________ was best known for inventing the first working telephone.

Bell was born in Edinburgh, Scotland, on March 3, 1847. During his youth, Bell was strongly (28) _________ by his family and his environment. Bell’s hometown of Edinburgh, Scotland, was known as the “Athens of the North” for its rich culture of arts and science.

By age 16, Alexander had joined his father in his work with the deaf. In 1870, the family settled in Brantford, Ontario, Canada. There, Alexander set up a workshop to continue his study of the human voice. On July 11, 1877, Bell married Mabel Hubbard who had been deaf (29) _________ her early childhood years.

Throughout his life, Bell continued his family’s work with the deaf. Bell died peacefully on August 2, 1922, at his home in Baddeck on Cape Breton Island, Nova Scotia, Canada.

sections.title: III. ĐỌC HIỂU - BÀI ĐỌC 3 (READING 3)
sections.instruction: Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C or D to indicate the correct answer to each of the questions.
sections.passage:
Steven Paul Jobs was born on 24 February, 1955 in San Francisco, USA. His biological parents were not married and gave him up for adoption. He was adopted by Clara and Paul Jobs. In 1971, Jobs met Steve Wozniak, who was five years older than him, but they bonded over their love of electronics. After high school, Jobs attended Reed College in Oregon, but found the classes boring and dropped out after six months.

When Jobs was 21, he and Wozniak started Apple Computers in Jobs' family garage with money they got by selling Jobs' van and Wozniak's scientific calculator. They turned it into a workspace where they built their first computers. By making computers smaller, cheaper, and accessible to everyday users, their company became a huge success and sales quickly increased.

Although Jobs left Apple in 1985, he returned to his post in 1997 when the company needed new ideas. He helped invent new products such as the iMac, the iBook for students, the iPod music player, and iTunes music software. In 2007, he introduced the touch-screen iPhone which changed the way phones were used. Apple products were not only designed to be cutting-edge technology, but also to be stylish and easy to use.

In addition, Jobs contributed to computer animation. In 1986, he bought a small company, which later became Pixar Animation Studios. It produced the first full-length computer-animated film Toy Story, followed by other blockbusters.

In 2003, Jobs was diagnosed with a rare form of pancreatic cancer. He fought the disease for several years, and stopped working in August, 2011. Two months later, he passed away. He had four children, three with his wife of 20 years and one from a previous relationship. On an Apple web page, a statement reads, "Apple has lost a visionary and creative genius, and the world has lost an amazing human being."

[Adapted from Global Success]

sections.title: III. ĐỌC HIỂU - BÀI ĐỌC 4 (READING 4)
sections.instruction: Read the following passage about Nguyen Du and choose the best answer for each question.
sections.passage:
Nguyen Du is a celebrated Vietnamese poet who wrote in Chữ Nôm, the ancient writing script of Viet Nam. His poetry is celebrated for the directness of its language and of its metaphors. Despite a number of Vietnamese poets pre-dated him, Nguyen Du is considered by many Vietnamese to be the founding-figure of Vietnamese literature. His epic poem Truyen Kieu (The Tale of Kieu), relating the brief and tragic life of a Vietnamese girl, is considered as a masterpiece.

Nguyen Du was born in 1765 in Tien Dien village, Nghi Xuan district, Nghe Tinh province, Viet Nam. By the age of 13, Nguyen had lost both of his parents, and for most of his teenage years he lived with his brother or with his brother-in-law.

At the age of 19, Nguyen passed the provincial examination. After that, he was appointed to the position of a military advisor in the Trinh army. After the Trinh Lords were defeated in 1786 by Nguyen Hue, Nguyen Du refused to serve in the new administration. He was arrested and held for some time before he moved back to his native village in the northern part of the country.

Later, when yet another warlord, Nguyen Anh, ruled Viet Nam in 1802, Nguyen Du agreed to serve in his administration. At first, he was given his old post of military advisor but after a decade, he was promoted to an ambassador to China in 1813.

While in China, he discovered and translated the Ming dynasty era tale “Kim Van Kieu” that would become the basis for the Tale of Kieu. He was later appointed to two more missions to Beijing, but before he could depart for the last one, he died of a long illness for which he refused treatment in 1820.

Nguyen Du’s father worked as a minister for the Lê dynasty, and his family did well during this time. However, Nguyen Du spent much of his life feeling guilty because he worked for a new ruler who took over, and he thought this was a betrayal of the true leaders of Viet Nam. He believed this brought dishonour to him and his family.

Mark the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the correct arrangement of the sentences to make a meaningful dialogue:
a. Anna: Definitely! Despite facing poverty and war, he always valued hard work and family above all.
b. Anna: Hi John, I often think about my grandfather. He lived through so many hardships and still managed to build a good life for his family.

d. John: Wow, that’s incredible. He must have been a strong and determined man.

Dear Teacher,
a. While I know he was committed to Vietnam’s independence, I would love to hear more about the challenges he faced and how he managed to stay resilient throughout.
b. Could you share some insights into his leadership during the revolutionary period, and what values guided his actions?
c. Recently, I’ve been reflecting on the life of President Ho Chi Minh, and I’m eager to learn more about his personal experiences.

John

sections.passage:
In the early twentieth century, an American woman named Emily Post wrote a book on etiquette. This book explained the (22)_____________behavior Americans should follow in many different social situations from birthday parties to funerals. But in modern society, it is not simply to know the proper rules for behavior in your own country. It is necessary for people (23) ________ work or travel abroad to understand the rules of etiquette in other cultures as well. Many cultural (24)______ can be found in such simple processes as giving or receiving a gift. In Western cultures, a gift can be given to the receiver with relatively little ceremony. When a gift is offered, the receiver usually takes the gift and expresses his or her thanks. (25)______, in some Asian countries, the act of gift-giving may appear confusing to Westerners. In Chinese culture, both the giver and receiver understand that the receiver will typically refuse to take the gift several times before he or she finally accepts it. In addition, to show respect (26)______ the receiver, it is common in several Asian cultures to use both hands when offering a gift to another person.

[Source: Reading Advantage by Casey Malarcher]

Festivals come with many traditions that bring happiness and joy to people around the world. They provide opportunities for families and friends to get together, enjoy exciting activities, and celebrate special occasions. However, some of these customs may not be environmentally friendly and may need to be changed for a (27) ______ future.

Balloons and sky lanterns
In countries such as China, India, and Japan, releasing balloons or sky lanterns provides (28)_________spectacular sight during festivals and other celebrations. People often release them to bring good luck, express their hopes, and send wishes to the sky. (29) ______, the litter left behind by balloons and lanterns is hard to decompose. The frames of the lanterns can harm wild animals, and many animals mistake the balloons (30) ______ food. Lanterns have also caused wildfires, putting forests, homes, and wildlife at risk. They can also cause fires, disturb wildlife, and frighten pets because of their loud noises. In addition, the smoke from fireworks may affect air quality and people's health.

To make festivals more environmentally friendly, communities can organise light shows, use reusable decorations, and encourage visitors to reduce waste. Small changes in traditional celebrations can help protect the environment for future generations.

sections.passageTitle: 60th Birthday Celebrations Across Cultures (Tiếng Anh 12 Bright)
sections.passage:
In many cultures around the world, turning sixty years old is a major milestone that represents wisdom, longevity, and a new stage of life. In countries like South Korea, Mexico, and India, people mark their 60th birthdays with special ceremonies, feasts, and family gatherings.

In South Korea, the 60th birthday, known as Hwangap, is highly significant. During this ceremony, children and younger relatives bow to their elders to show respect and wish them well. The birthday person shares a meal with family, including traditional dishes like rice cakes and miyeok guk (seaweed soup). They also receive blessings and good wishes.

In Mexico, turning sixty is called la fiesta de sesenta cumpleaños. The celebration often includes a religious blessing from a local priest, followed by the exchange of gifts and a festive meal. Traditional foods such as mole—a rich sauce made with chilli and chocolate—and pastel de tres leches, a soft cake soaked in three kinds of milk, are commonly served.

In India, many people celebrate their 60th birthday with a ceremony called Sashti Poorthi. It features prayer rituals to wish the person health and prosperity. Relatives and friends enjoy dishes like lentil soup and biryani, a flavorful rice and meat dish. Gifts of gold jewellery are often given to honour the elder.

These celebrations of longevity remind people of the wisdom and guidance of their elders. They bring families together to express gratitude, respect, and love toward parents and grandparents who have contributed greatly to their families and communities.

[Tiếng Anh 12 Bright]

sections.passageTitle: Chinese Gift-Giving Etiquette (Adapted from Regina Coeli)
sections.passage:
When the British transport minister presented a watch to a Chinese official, her act was described by BBC as a “cultural gaffe”. So why is a “watch” not a good gift in Chinese eyes? And what are the right and wrong choices for gifts to Chinese business associates and friends? The answer lies in the Chinese language.

Giving someone a clock or a watch as a present is traditionally a taboo in Chinese culture due to “giving a clock” and “attending a person’s funeral” having the same pronunciation, regardless of the different written characters. Therefore, avoiding presenting a gift which has “the same pronunciation of any unlucky meaning” is important in building relationships with Chinese people.

Gifts are presented with two hands in China. The receiving person may decline the gift at first (or even up to three times). It is part of the custom for Chinese to do so as they consider themselves not worthy of the gift. However, do not withdraw the gift as your persistent trying will persuade the Chinese into accepting your gift. If presenting organisational gifts, it is done during a toast or at the end of a meal, just prior to departure. In modern time China, sometimes a business meeting is planned on short notice and can be quite short. In this case, organisational gifts are exchanged after the first speaker of meeting parties or just before the end of the meeting.

[Adapted from Regina Coeli]

sections.passageTitle: Functions and Nutritional Value of Fats
sections.passage:
Most human diets contain between 10 and 15 percent of their total calories as protein. The rest of the dietary energy comes from carbohydrates, fats, and in some people, alcohol. The proportion of calories from fats varies from 10 percent in poor communities to 40 percent or more in rich communities.

In addition to providing energy, fats have several other functions in the body. The fat-soluble vitamins, A, D, E, and K, are dissolved in fats, as their name implies. Good sources of these vitamins have high oil or fat content, and the vitamins are stored in the body’s fatty tissues. In the diet, fats cause food to remain longer in the stomach, thus increasing the feeling of fullness for some time after a meal is eaten. Fats add variety, taste, and texture to foods, which accounts for the popularity of fried foods. Fatty deposits in the body have an insulating and protective value. The curves of the female human body are due mostly to strategically located fat deposits.

Whether a certain amount of fat in the diet is essential to human health is not definitely known. When rats are fed a fat-free diet, their growth eventually ceases, their skin becomes inflamed and scaly, and their reproductive systems are damaged. Two fatty acids, linoleic and arachidonic acids, prevent these abnormalities and hence are called essential fatty acids. They are required by a number of other animals, but their roles in human beings are debatable. Most nutritionists consider linoleic fatty acid an essential nutrient for humans.

sections.passageTitle: The Generation Gap in the Modern Business World
sections.passage:
The generation gap in the business world is a fascinating phenomenon that highlights the differences in attitudes, values, and approaches to conducting business between different generations. One of the key areas where the generation gap is evident is in technology adoption. Younger generations, such as Millennials and Generation Z, have grown up in the digital age and are generally more comfortable with technology. They readily embrace new tools, platforms, and digital strategies, which can significantly impact business practices, marketing strategies, and communication methods.

Workforce expectations also play a crucial role in the generation gap. Each generation has its own set of expectations when it comes to work-life balance, career progression, and job satisfaction. Younger generations often prioritize flexibility, purpose-driven work, and a healthy work-life balance. Meanwhile, older generations may place more emphasis on job stability, loyalty, and traditional career paths.

Leadership styles are another area where the generation gap becomes evident. Baby Boomers and Generation X typically favor hierarchical structures and a more top-down management style. They are used to a more authoritative approach to leadership. Conversely, younger generations often prefer collaborative and inclusive leadership styles, valuing input from all levels of the organization. They thrive in environments that encourage participation, teamwork, and innovation.

Communication preferences have also evolved with each generation. The way people communicate and consume information has drastically changed over the years. Younger generations are inclined towards instant messaging, social media, and other digital channels for communication.

Mệnh đề trạng ngữ chỉ thời gian với "While" diễn tả một hành động đang diễn ra trong quá khứ ("last summer"): "While I was working...".
Rút gọn mệnh đề quan hệ dạng chủ động (who are living): "The lovely kids living in this small shelter...".
Cụm từ "provide sth to sb" (cung cấp sự hỗ trợ thực tế và đồ dùng thiết yếu cho trẻ em).
Cụm động từ "set up" có nghĩa là tổ chức, thiết lập (set up charity shows: tổ chức các chương trình biểu diễn từ thiện).
Cụm danh từ "financial donations" (khoản quyên góp tài chính hảo tâm).
Cần tính từ miêu tả ứng dụng tập luyện: "successful exercise application" (ứng dụng thể thao thành công).
Cấu trúc so sánh nhất: "the most popular fitness network" (mạng lưới thể dục thể thao phổ biến nhất).
Liên từ chỉ sự nhượng bộ phù hợp về ngữ nghĩa: "Although the company faces fierce competition..." (Mặc dù phải đối mặt với sự cạnh tranh khốc liệt...).
Động từ khuyết thiếu diễn tả kế hoạch tương lai gần: "the business will introduce..." (doanh nghiệp sẽ sớm giới thiệu các tính năng mới).
Đại từ bất định chỉ người: "Anyone using the app can track their health metrics..." (Bất kỳ ai sử dụng ứng dụng đều có thể theo dõi...).

options.text: Pharmacogenomics helps prevent negative reactions to medications
Analyzing tumor mutations has contributed to decreased mortality in some cancers
Genomic research currently suffers from a lack of demographic diversity
Personalized medicine relies solely on a patient's genetic data to cure diseases

questions.explanation: Tác giả KHÔNG đồng ý với nhận định D: y học cá nhân hóa không chỉ dựa vào dữ liệu gen để chữa khỏi hoàn toàn mà còn tính đến lối sống, hệ vi sinh vật và thói quen sinh hoạt hằng ngày.

questions.explanation: Từ "undermining" (làm suy yếu, hủy hoại) có từ TRÁI NGHĨA là "Bolstering" (củng cố, tăng cường, gia cố sức mạnh).

questions.questionText: In which paragraph does the writer point out the demographic limitations of current genomic databases?
questions.explanation: Ở đoạn 4 tác giả chỉ rõ hạn chế về dữ liệu chủng tộc: "A disproportionate number of genomic studies lean heavily on individuals of European descent..." (phần lớn nghiên cứu gen thiên lệch về người gốc châu Âu).

Criticizing the overuse of antibiotics in clinical cancer trials
Outlining the dietary habits that prevent tumor metastasis in mice
Explaining how gut bacteria manipulation informs cancer treatment strategies

questions.explanation: Ở đoạn 1, tác giả đang giải thích cách thức việc điều chỉnh vi khuẩn đường ruột cung cấp thông tin định hướng cho các phác đồ điều trị ung thư.

options.text: Tailoring strategies to individual patients is less effective than applying standard protocols in contemporary oncology
Modern oncology prefers strict, uniform guidelines because they are safer than personalized biological treatments
Contemporary cancer care eschews generalized methods in favor of treatments customized to individual genetic profiles
The biological signature of each patient is ignored when blanket protocols are applied in modern cancer therapies

questions.explanation: Câu gạch chân nhấn mạnh ung thư học hiện đại không dùng phác đồ đại trà mà điều chỉnh liệu pháp theo dấu ấn sinh học riêng của từng người ➔ Khớp hoàn toàn với C: "Contemporary cancer care eschews generalized methods in favor of treatments customized to individual genetic profiles".

questions.explanation: Ở đoạn 3, tác giả nói về lĩnh vực dược lý di truyền (pharmacogenomics) đối chiếu đơn thuốc với đặc điểm di truyền của bệnh nhân để kiểm tra độ tương thích.

options.text: Participation Income rewards societal contributions that fall outside traditional employment metrics.
Post-work guarantees are primarily designed to dismantle existing labor markets and market ideologies.
Universal Basic Services aims to entirely replace the need for direct cash transfers to citizens.
Conventional welfare systems successfully encourage individuals to accept low-wage jobs by maintaining benefits.

questions.explanation: Thông tin A đúng theo đoạn 2: "Participation Income broadens the definition of productivity by adequately remunerating unpaid care and civic engagement..." (ghi nhận những đóng góp xã hội nằm ngoài các chỉ số việc làm truyền thống).

options.text: Marginalized communities prefer cash transfers over public services because market-first systems already provide affordable essential care.
UBS advocates for the collective provision of essential services to lower individuals' living costs and reduce the necessity for large cash stipends.
High-quality public infrastructure is overly expensive to maintain, making Universal Basic Services an unviable alternative to direct cash.
Market-first ideologies have completely failed, forcing governments to privatize healthcare and public transit to stabilize living standards.

questions.explanation: Đoạn 3 nhấn mạnh: Dịch vụ Cơ bản Phổ quát (UBS) vận động cung cấp tập thể các nhu yếu phẩm để giảm gánh nặng chi phí sinh hoạt cho người dân, từ đó giảm quy mô trợ cấp tiền mặt cần thiết. Đáp án B.

questions.explanation: Đại từ "they" ở đoạn 2 chỉ "households" (các hộ gia đình).

options.text: The Downfall of Free Markets: Why Universal Basic Income Fails
Macroeconomic Volatility: The Hidden Costs of Public Infrastructure
Rethinking Livelihoods: The Case for Post-Work Guarantees
Eradicating Labor: How Participation Income Replaces Employment

questions.explanation: Tiêu đề toàn diện và sâu sắc nhất cho bài đọc: Rethinking Livelihoods: The Case for Post-Work Guarantees (Tái tư duy sinh kế: Lập luận cho các đảm bảo sau việc làm).

questions.questionText: Where in the passage does the following sentence best fit? By removing the punitive threat of sudden welfare withdrawal, the system encourages genuine economic mobility.
questions.explanation: Câu cần chèn nói về việc loại bỏ mối đe dọa đột ngột cắt trợ cấp để khuyến khích dịch chuyển kinh tế, phù hợp nhất với vị trí [II] ngay sau khi nhắc đến "benefit cliff".

questions.questionText: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?

options.text: Unconditional welfare stipends inherently discourage citizens from pursuing any form of paid employment or skill development.
The primary goal of Participation Income is to force individuals into unpaid community care roles against their will.
Post-work guarantees require the complete eradication of private enterprise to adequately fund Universal Basic Services.
The financial feasibility of a basic income is inversely related to the quality and availability of public services.

questions.explanation: Suy luận từ đoạn 3: Tính khả thi tài chính của một khoản thu nhập cơ bản tỷ lệ nghịch với chất lượng và tính sẵn có của các dịch vụ công cộng. Đáp án D.

questions.questionText: According to paragraph 1, the primary objective of post-work guarantees is to _____

options.text: force vulnerable demographics to participate in civic duties
replace all existing welfare models with conditional stipends
completely dismantle the traditional labor market framework
secure an inviolable baseline of living standards for all citizens

questions.explanation: Theo đoạn 1, mục tiêu cốt lõi của post-work guarantees là bảo đảm một nền tảng chuẩn mức sống không thể xâm phạm cho mọi công dân. Đáp án D.

questions.questionText: What conclusion can be drawn from paragraph 2?

options.text: Eliminating the conditionalities of traditional welfare helps mitigate poverty traps and recognizes broader forms of civic value.
Traditional employment metrics perfectly capture and remunerate all forms of productive labor within modern economic systems.
Tax-free stipends should only be distributed to individuals who actively participate in unpaid community care and civic engagement.
Benefit cliffs are an essential mechanism for motivating households to seek higher-paying jobs in the traditional labor market.

questions.explanation: Kết luận từ đoạn 2: Loại bỏ các điều kiện ràng buộc khắt khe của phúc lợi truyền thống giúp giảm bớt bẫy nghèo đói và công nhận nhiều dạng giá trị cống hiến cho xã hội. Đáp án A.

questions.questionText: The word alleviate in paragraph 3 is OPPOSITE in meaning to _____.
questions.explanation: Từ "alleviate" (làm giảm nhẹ bớt) có từ TRÁI NGHĨA là "exacerbate" (làm trầm trọng thêm, làm tồi tệ hơn).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT implied in paragraph 4?

options.text: Reducing the necessity of coerced labor can yield positive dividends for the environment.
Individuals currently face pressure to prioritize economic growth over their own well-being.
Having guaranteed survival allows citizens to distribute their time across varied meaningful pursuits.
Post-work guarantees will inevitably lead to a drastic reduction in national productivity.

questions.explanation: Ở đoạn 4 tác giả chỉ ra động lực tài chính khi chi phí nông dược tăng vọt khiến nông dân phải áp dụng hệ thống bón phân biến thiên để thắt lưng buộc bụng: Paragraph 4.

questions.explanation: Ở đoạn 3 tác giả mô tả công nghệ thế hệ mới gắn cảm biến trực tiếp vào máy móc để đo đạc và xử lý ngay tại chỗ mà không cần bản đồ số lập trình sẵn: Paragraph 3.

questions.explanation: Từ "These" ở đoạn 3 thay thế cho các hệ thống công nghệ chính xác tiên tiến: "Advanced precision technologies".

questions.explanation: Từ "uniform" (đồng nhất, đơn điệu, giống nhau một khuôn) có từ TRÁI NGHĨA là "Heterogeneous" (đa dạng, không đồng nhất, hỗn hợp nhiều thành phần).

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements would the writer NOT agree with?

options.text: Early agricultural mechanization maximized input efficiency while substantially cutting down on manual labor costs
Site-specific management treats the natural diversity of farmland as an asset rather than a problem
Modern precision farming captures the meticulous attention to detail characteristic of traditional cultivation
The integration of drone signals and soil chemistry data allows for the creation of precise management blueprints

questions.explanation: Tác giả KHÔNG đồng ý với nhận định A vì đoạn 4 nêu rõ: cơ giới hóa ban đầu tuy giảm chi phí nhân công nhưng làm tổn hại nghiêm trọng đến hiệu quả sử dụng vật tư đầu vào.

questions.questionText: Which of the following best paraphrases the underlined sentence in paragraph 2? Question. Decision-making is firmly rooted in hard evidence rather than guesswork, ensuring interventions are perfectly in sync with the equipment's exact location.

options.text: Empirical evidence suggests that modern farming equipment operates independently without requiring specific locational sync
Farmers rely heavily on intuition to decide where machinery should be placed, reducing the need for hard evidence
Agricultural actions are dictated by precise empirical data, aligning chemical treatments exactly with the machinery's physical position
Guesswork has been entirely eliminated from farming, meaning machines now make all strategic decisions autonomously

questions.explanation: Câu gạch chân khẳng định: Việc ra quyết định dựa chắc chắn vào dữ liệu thực nghiệm thay vì phỏng đoán, bảo đảm các biện pháp can thiệp đồng bộ chính xác với vị trí máy móc ➔ Khớp hoàn toàn với C.

questions.questionText: In paragraph 1, the writer is ______.

options.text: Criticizing modern farmers for intentionally polluting local groundwater systems
Highlighting the ecological and financial drawbacks of conventional uniform farming methods
Advocating for a complete return to manual labor to prevent chemical runoff
Explaining the chemical composition of fertilizers used in blanket agricultural approaches

questions.explanation: Ở đoạn 1, tác giả nêu bật các nhược điểm về sinh thái và tài chính của phương pháp canh tác đồng loạt truyền thống: Đáp án B.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true according to the passage?

options.text: Digital twins are primarily implemented to mask the adverse distributive impacts of urban policies from residents
Civic engagement in digital simulations significantly delays essential maintenance, eventually triggering full-blown and irreversible urban crises
Integrating sensor data automatically resolves all complex infrastructure anomalies without requiring any active human administrative intervention
Integrating public feedback into digital models shifts urban decision-making from mere intuition to rigorous empirical justification

questions.explanation: Thông tin D đúng theo đoạn 3: Việc tích hợp phản hồi của người dân vào mô hình số chuyển đổi việc ra quyết định quản trị đô thị từ trực giác cảm tính sang các căn cứ thực nghiệm nghiêm ngặt.

questions.questionText: The word they refers to _____.
questions.explanation: Đại từ "they" ở đoạn 3 thay thế cho "Administrators" (các nhà quản lý đô thị).

questions.questionText: Which of the following best summarises paragraph 3?

options.text: Digital twins eliminate the need for human administrators by autonomously running flood evacuation drills and retiming traffic lights
The primary purpose of digital twins is simply to justify aftermarket rationalizations through the appearance of technological sophistication
Public feedback is generally considered excessively subjective to be integrated into objective data streams from real-time sensors
By relying on empirical evidence and community input, digital twins enforce accountability and ensure models match practical realities

questions.explanation: Tóm tắt đoạn 3: Nhờ dựa vào chứng cứ thực nghiệm và ý kiến cộng đồng, bản sao số nâng cao trách nhiệm giải trình và đảm bảo các mô hình phản ánh sát thực tế. Đáp án D.

questions.questionText: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?

options.text: As digital twins become increasingly sophisticated, the essential necessity for public deliberation will proportionally and steadily decrease
The concept of a digital twin citizen was initially developed to surveil residents rather than empower them
Cities declining to implement digital twins will inevitably face insurmountable economic decay and complete catastrophic infrastructural collapse
Open access to urban simulations fosters a collaborative governance structure, significantly mitigating the risks of unilateral decision-making

questions.explanation: Suy luận từ bài đọc: Việc mở rộng tiếp cận các mô hình mô phỏng đô thị thúc đẩy cơ chế đồng quản trị, giảm thiểu đáng kể nguy cơ ra quyết định đơn phương. Đáp án D.

questions.questionText: According to paragraph 1, digital twins allow stakeholders to _____

options.text: Predict the exact financial costs of routine maintenance without any calculating error
Evaluate the potential ramifications of urban policies prior to physical implementation
Replace human administrators entirely to balance finite resources without human intervention
Construct physical infrastructure significantly faster than traditional methods of urban development

questions.explanation: Theo đoạn 1, digital twins cho phép các bên liên quan đánh giá trước tác động của các chính sách đô thị trước khi tiến hành xây dựng trên thực tế. Đáp án B.

questions.questionText: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?

The Illusion of Control: Why Digital Twins Fail to Reflect Realities
The Impending Obsolescence of the Digital Twin Citizen in City Administration

questions.explanation: Tiêu đề phù hợp và giàu tính học thuật nhất: Virtual Replicas and Civic Voices: Deducting New Eras of Urban Governance (Bản sao ảo và tiếng nói công dân: Định hình kỷ nguyên mới của quản trị đô thị).

questions.questionText: The word reckless in paragraph 3 is OPPOSITE in meaning to _____.

questions.questionText: What conclusion can be drawn from paragraph 4?

options.text: Transparent, evidence-based urban planning effectively strengthens the social contract between city authorities and their local constituents
Residents are predominantly interested in identifying administrative blind spots to criticize authorities rather than co-producing governance
Technological marvels are entirely valuable only if they completely automate the governance and investment prioritization processes
The cold light of day inevitably exposes the fatal flaws inherent in utilizing digital management models

questions.explanation: Kết luận từ đoạn 4: Quy hoạch đô thị minh bạch dựa trên bằng chứng củng cố mạnh mẽ sự gắn kết xã hội và niềm tin giữa chính quyền thành phố và người dân. Đáp án A.

Ground-truthing simulations utilizing residents' authentic experiences helps prevent relatively minor issues from worsening into crises
Residents must possess advanced technical skills to meaningfully engage with the digital twin's complex dashboards
Interactive dashboards serve as an effective tool for communities to critically evaluate proposed urban projects
